<h2>Diagnose the sjSDM Setup</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Comprehensive non-aborting diagnosis of the sjSDM installation, including
Python, PyTorch, CUDA support, and sjSDM functionality.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>diagnose_sjsdm_setup(run_test_model = base::interactive())
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="run_test_model">run_test_model</code></td>
<td>
<p>Logical. Should a test model be fitted to
diagnose full functionality? Defaults to 'interactive()'.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>This function performs the following checks:
1. Interactive runtime availability
2. Python version and location
3. PyTorch installation and version
4. CUDA/GPU availability
5. sjSDM package installation
6. sjSDM Python dependencies
7. Test model fitting (optional)
</p>
<p>All checks print their status with [OK], [WARN], or [FAIL]. Failures are
represented in the returned list rather than raised as errors.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>Invisible list with diagnostic results. Called primarily for
side effects.
</p>


<h3>See Also</h3>

<p><code>py_config</code>
<code>sjSDM</code>
</p>

</main>
